name: Hiwot
text: [breathless] {target}! Oh, thank every saint that listens. I saw you both leave and I followed — yes, I know, I was not supposed to — and then I saw the torches, and the big one in the black armour, and I ran the other way, because I am not brave. I am only fast.

name: Hiwot
text: [quieter] He is dead. Tesfaye. I saw him fall. I can't believe we left him there. He should be with us.

name: Hiwot
text: [urgent] Tell me what the big one said to him. I was too far; I saw his mouth move and Tesfaye shake his head. What did he want?

name: Hiwot
text: [steadying] He wanted you. By name. Then it was never about Tesfaye at all. — Close. Yes. I can do close. I have his letter; it was in his coat. An inn on the Shore Road, and two names, Beau and Delphine. He must have meant for us to go to them.

name: Hiwot
text: [stung, then flat] Right. I am fine. — I have his letter. An inn and two names. You may read it when you have finished being a wall.

name: Hiwot
text: [uneasy] "What you are." He said that? — You sounded like him just then. Not Tesfaye. The other one. [softer] There is a letter. An inn, two names. Let us go and be alive first. You can be terrible later.

name: Hiwot
text: [firm] I am coming with you. I can pick locks and keep watch while you sleep. Besides, if you leave me here, I will only have to follow you again.

name: Hiwot
text: [reading] "The Open Hand, on the Shore Road, past the salt-flats. Ask for Beau and Delphine. They are Wardens, and they were my friends before you were born. Trust them as you would trust me." — That is all it says. He never wasted ink.

name: Hiwot
text: [thinking] Wardens. He never once said that word in twenty years, and now it is the first thing he wants us to know. That is the first thing I am asking them.

name: Hiwot
text: [low, to you] Do not tell them anything. We do not know them.

name: Hiwot
text: [low] Wolves. Road wolves, the big grey kind — Tesfaye said they only come down to the road when the hills are hungry.

name: Hiwot
text: [very quiet] Something has made the hills hungry.

name: Hiwot
text: [sceptical] Alone. Who sends one squire to a wolf den? What did you do to your Order?

name: Hiwot
text: [quickly] Neither. We are pilgrims. Going to the shrine at — the shrine.

name: Hiwot
text: [picking up the paper] He was carrying this. Your face, and a bounty, and a seal of an iron hand in red wax. No name.

name: Hiwot
text: [quiet] Somebody with a great deal of money wants you dead badly enough to send two men in one night and a third to wait at the one door Tesfaye trusted. I am keeping this. Somebody at that inn will know the mark.

name: Hiwot
text: [thinking] A locked drawer in his study. I never got it open, and I tried twice, which he knew, because he moved the key. He never moved anything else.

name: Hiwot
text: [quiet] It is still there. Whatever it is.

name: Hiwot
text: [low] It smells like wet dog and hot metal. Four levels of that, going down.

name: Hiwot
text: [quiet] Keep your light up. I can't see where these stairs end.

name: Hiwot
text: [reading] "Keep the ore fouled until the spring shipment. Gorruk holds the north road." And a name — Femi, at the inn in Thornbury.

name: Hiwot
text: [quiet] Tesfaye died over a shipping schedule. That cannot be the whole of it. It cannot.

name: Hiwot
text: [quiet, at the fire] Delphine. Was he a good Warden? Tesfaye. He never talked about it, and I have been wondering all day whether that was because it was bad, or because it was good.

name: Hiwot
text: [murmuring] Map, seal, and a very old sausage. He did not feel a thing.

name: Hiwot
text: [low] Past Holloway Vale, under the oaks. There is a note about the road being watched.

name: Hiwot
text: [whispering] Or I go over the palisade and open the back gate while every eye is on the front.

name: Hiwot
text: [breathless] The back gate is open. Two sentries were sleeping, and one of them is going to wake with a headache and no boots.

name: Hiwot
text: [low] The big tent is the lord's. There is a man chained in it who looks as though he still has jokes left.

name: Hiwot
text: [resigned] Loud, then. Go for the one with the horns first; the rest will look to him.

name: Hiwot
text: [low] Old trees. Very old, very big. Things in the branches that stop moving when we look.

name: Hiwot
text: [a breath] I will go first. No. I will not. You go first.

name: Hiwot
text: [appalled] It has a sting on its tail. Its tail has a sting.

name: Hiwot
text: [sick] They keep them in cages between shifts. Like dogs. Worse than dogs; I have seen dogs kept better than this.

name: Hiwot
text: [frantic] Beau is below with the chain-gang. If you turn that wheel he drowns with them.

name: Hiwot
text: [shouting] NO —

name: Hiwot
text: [hollow] He was coming up. We could hear the chains.

name: Hiwot
text: [reading] Three names at the Consortium's tower in the city. Adigun Adeyinka, Bankole, Rotimi.

name: Hiwot
text: [quiet] The road north is open now. There is nothing between us and the Gate but the Gate.

name: Hiwot
text: [low] The druids wanted this mine shut down too.

name: Hiwot
text: [dry] We could have had their help. Instead, we picked a fight with them. That was clever of us.

name: Hiwot
text: [gagging] I have been in a mine, a fortress and a spider nest this month, and THIS is the worst. This is the worst place.

name: Hiwot
text: [whispering] Doorman. I can get us past him. He will not even remember we were here.

name: Hiwot
text: [smug] Side window. He is asleep on his feet. I told you.

name: Hiwot
text: [sighing] Loud again. I am keeping a list.

name: Hiwot
text: [horrified] That is the merchant's face. That is his FACE and it is not him. Nothing is behind the eyes.

name: Hiwot
text: [whispering] A clerk. Two guards. A very long list of names on his desk, and we are not on it.

name: Hiwot
text: [impressed] He BELIEVED you. Olamide's name still opens doors. Third floor, he says. Do not touch anything.

name: Hiwot
text: [flat] So much for quiet. Stairs. Go.

name: Hiwot
text: [hushed] Got it. There is a name at the bottom in red: "the ward — as agreed." Whatever we do up there, somebody upstairs already knows we are coming.

name: Hiwot
text: [stunned] Lanternhold. They went HOME. The three men who paid to kill Tesfaye are sitting in his library. — The drawer. Delphine, the locked drawer. We are going to be in that room.

name: Hiwot
text: [suspicious] How did you know Tesfaye? I lived in that keep twenty years and I never once saw you.

name: Hiwot
text: [flat] That is not an answer.

name: Hiwot
text: [strange] It smells the same. Ink and dust and the brothers' lentils. I thought it would feel like home, and it feels like a trap.

name: Hiwot
text: [brightly] None of us. We are pilgrims.

name: Hiwot
text: [Hiwot's voice, wrong] {target}. Thank the saints. I got separated — come here, come HERE, we have to go —

name: Hiwot
text: [the real Hiwot, furious] The HONEY. It was the honey, and Brother Yonas still blames the cat — that thing wearing my face does not know that, so STAB IT.

name: Hiwot
text: [shaking] Out. We are out. I am never going home again, am I.

name: Hiwot
text: [small] Sanni sent us into that room. Then he told the guards we'd murdered his father. He had this planned before we ever left the city.

name: Hiwot
text: [reading] "Wanted, for the murder of Grand Duke Ayodele and of the Consortium summit at Lanternhold: the ward of Tesfaye, and company." That is your face. That is a BAD drawing of your face.

name: Hiwot
text: [quiet] The street is full of it: Emeka Obi is dead. A man called Segun Marr commands the Gauntlet now, and he is the one who signed this.

name: Hiwot
text: [thinking] Three doors. Adebayo, if we can save him. Folake, if you can stand her. Or Tunde Softfoot and a debt.

name: Hiwot
text: [nodding] The Duke. All right. I like a Duke who owes us.

name: Hiwot
text: [uneasy] Folake. I do not trust her smile. I do not trust anything about her. But she does have a door.

name: Hiwot
text: [grinning] Tunde! Yes. I was hoping you would say that. Thieves are honest about what they are.

name: Hiwot
text: [itching] I hate silk. I hate silk SO much. — There he is. On the dais. Smiling. He has a lovely smile. I want to put it through a wall.

name: Hiwot
text: [shouting] The dukes — {target}, the DUKES — we cannot hold them if you run at him —

name: Hiwot
text: [stiff, bandaged] I heard you were going under the city without me. Absolutely not.

name: Hiwot
text: [fierce] I am stitched, I am furious, and I still open locks better than anyone here. Move over.

name: Hiwot
text: [hushed] The thieves' maze. I can read it — half of it is Lanternhold locks, the cheap kind. Follow me exactly.

name: Hiwot
text: [murmuring] Left. Again. Not that one. — Through. Nobody bled. Tell Tesfaye I was paying attention.

name: Hiwot
text: [groaning] Straight through. Fine. The loud list is getting long.

name: Hiwot
text: [whispering] It is warm down here. It should not be warm.

name: Hiwot
text: [fierce] Whatever he says in there — you are Tesfaye's. Not his. Tesfaye's.

name: Hiwot
text: [horrified] That is ME. That is all of us. They are wearing US.

name: Hiwot
text: [shouting] The left one! The left one is looking at YOU!

name: Hiwot
text: [breathless] Still with you. Keep going!

name: Hiwot
text: [gleeful] Got his purse. And his knife. And his — never mind, keep fighting.

name: Hiwot
text: [urgent] The marks on the floor! They lead to the altar. Get away from them!

name: Hiwot
text: [shocked] No. Let go of me!

name: Hiwot
text: [weak] I can hear you. He has bound me to the throne. Break his hold before he can finish.

name: Hiwot
text: [quiet] He’s gone. I can feel the power he took, and yours. It is holding this place open.

name: Hiwot
text: [steady] If you let it all go, I can come back with you. You will lose Morrak’s blood, and any claim to his throne. If you keep it, you can take his place. I cannot come back that way.

name: Hiwot
text: [unsteady] I can breathe. I thought I would never...

name: Hiwot
text: [soft] You came back for me. Let’s get out of here. Please.

name: Hiwot
text: [quiet] I wanted to go home with you. I hope you remember that.

name: Desmond
text: [bright] Well now — look at this, Winston. Two little travellers on a big empty road, and one of them holding a sword like it might bite.

name: Desmond
text: [delighted] Desmond. This is Winston. We are going the same way as you, which is a coincidence, and we are very good in a fight, which is not.

name: Desmond
text: [gleeful] Lying. Look at the hands, Winston — the hands always know. I like them already.

name: Desmond
text: [sing-song] No worry yourself. Everybody lies to us. We are used to it.

name: Desmond
text: [sing-song] You hear that, Winston? We have friends now. — No worry yourself, {target}. I bite only the ones you tell me to.

name: Desmond
text: [soft] Those papers. Names, seals, routes. The people we answer to would pay plenty to read them before the Gauntlet does.

name: Desmond
text: [softer] Let Winston copy them tonight, and we stay quiet and useful for as long as you like.

name: Desmond
text: [very calm] Then we go, and you will see us again, and it won't be as friends.

name: Desmond
text: [light] It never was, really. I did tell you stories like yours get told badly.

name: Desmond
text: [bright] {target}! You found us! We work here now, you see it? It pays better than you did.

name: Desmond
text: [giggling] Winston says we should kill you quick. Me, I would like to take my time.

name: Desmond
text: [giggling] Oh, he is BURNING. Look at him go, man.

name: Desmond
text: [sing-song] More, more, more —

name: Desmond
text: [delighted] Come on, then. I'm right here.

name: Winston
text: [flat] He talks. I do the rest.

name: Winston
text: [level] Before anybody says yes or no: where are two children walking so fast, with one blade between them and no pack? People with a reason walk like that. I want the reason.

name: Winston
text: [thoughtful] The Open Hand. That's a Warden house; everybody on this coast knows it. So you are walking toward trouble, not away from it, and you are honest about it. Both of those are useful to me.

name: Winston
text: [unbothered] Fair. It is. Then here is mine, so we are even.

name: Winston
text: [flat] We are hired blades between hirings, and the road is bad for two and better for four. Say yes or say no, but say it before the light goes. I do not like this stretch after dark.

name: Winston
text: [dry] You want the true answer or the polite one? Polite: two men with skills and no master this month. True: we work for people who pay to know things, and right now they would like to know why iron costs three times what it did last year. You are not the thing we are looking for. You are on the road to it.

name: Winston
text: [a sigh] Desmond is well the way a fire is well. He can raise the dead for a little while and he laughs when the dead fall down again. I keep him pointed the right way. I have done it since we were boys and I am tired, but I am still doing it.

name: Winston
text: [unbothered] Then go easy. If you change your mind, we will be the ones ahead of you with the fire lit. — Desmond. Walk.

name: Winston
text: [flat] Before the knives, girl. What's the rate? Two hundred, still, or has it gone up since Merle?

name: Winston
text: [dry] Thinking about who can afford to keep raising it. Carry on.

name: Winston
text: [flat] Mayor. Who takes your wagons north? One buyer, or many?

name: Winston
text: [low, to himself] One buyer. That's what they wanted to know. — Go on, man.

name: Winston
text: [firm] That chief keeps healing. I've shut it off for now. Hit him before it wears off.

name: Winston
text: [flat] Which spring shipment, priest? Whose wagons?

name: Winston
text: [calm] Three ways into a camp like that, man. Loud, quiet, or invited.

name: Winston
text: [dry] Desmond and I can be invited. Recruiters never look too close at faces that frighten them.

name: Winston
text: [murmuring] Walk like you already killed somebody today. Desmond — no smiling.

name: Winston
text: [low] We are in. The big tent is Gorruk's. There is a chained man inside; don't look at him yet.

name: Winston
text: [flat] Loud. Sawa — fine. The one with the horns is a sergeant; the rest look to him. Kill him first and they look to nobody.

name: Winston
text: [flat] Two sets of books, mage. Which one goes to the Gate?

name: Winston
text: [flat] He means it. So do I. It is the only thing we were ever on this road for, and I told you I would say so before the day came. This is the day.

name: Winston
text: [level] The Umbral Hand. You have heard the name; everybody has, and everybody pretends they haven't. Merchants, mostly, of a kind. They want to know who is cornering iron on this coast, and why, and they don't much care who dies of the knowing.

name: Winston
text: [nodding] Copies. Fair. You won't regret keeping us.

name: Winston
text: [dry] You may regret Desmond. That is a separate matter.

name: Winston
text: [flat] Doorman. Leave him to me. Everybody has a price, and his is written on his face.

name: Winston
text: [flat] Thirty gold and the man has gone for a very long lunch.

name: Winston
text: [dry] Through him, then. Mind — a man that size falls slow.

name: Winston
text: [flat] Nothing personal, man. You said that yourself once.

name: Winston
text: [flat] Back lane. Poison. Done.

name: Winston
text: [calm] Stay close. Don't give them a gap.

name: Winston
text: [dry] Desmond, stop laughing, it puts them off.

name: Santiago
text: [formal, out of breath] Wait! Wolves in that den. Give me a moment. I ran all the way from the bend.

name: Santiago
text: [straightening] Santiago. I'm a squire with the Order of the Dawning Flame. They sent me to clear this road. No, there's no one else coming.

name: Santiago
text: [reddening, honest] Nothing! This is my first errand. They said the road was quiet. I counted the tracks outside that den twice. Please don't tell the Order I asked for help.

name: Santiago
text: [honest] I've only fought in the training yard. Straw doesn't come at you in a pack. Could you stay?

name: Santiago
text: [earnest] Knights sworn to the sun. Our chapter house is down in the sun-lands, where I grew up. I still turn east when I pray, even under all these trees. They sent me north to learn the roads. I hadn't expected to be grateful for strangers this soon.

name: Santiago
text: [reddening, then honest] Sword practice. Prayers. They didn't put teeth on the practice dummy. With respect, are you going to help?

name: Santiago
text: [relieved] God keep you. Give me a moment to tighten this strap. All right. Stay behind my shield.

name: Santiago
text: [formal, hurt] I see. God go with you. I'll wait until they come out. One at a time, I hope.

name: Santiago
text: [uneasy] Burning Gauntlet. What's a city patrol doing down here? They've got a woman at sword-point. I don't recognise her dress.

name: Santiago
text: [formal, tight] Which goddess, señora? Tell me her name before I draw my weapon.

name: Santiago
text: [quietly] Yes, it matters to me. {target}, are we stepping in? I'll follow your lead here.

name: Santiago
text: [quietly] I've prayed over this every night. I still can't accept the company we're keeping. If I stay, we'll have this same argument at every fire. I'm leaving.

name: Santiago
text: [formal] I'll be at the Open Hand. If you part ways with them, come and find me. I'd like to ride with you again. God keep you, {target}.

name: Santiago
text: [low] Let her wait. You don't owe her an answer just because she's frightened.

name: Santiago
text: [hesitant] In the yard, you could put your hand up and stop the bout. I miss that.

name: Santiago
text: [honest] I pray before we fight. Then I look for somewhere to run. Haven't done it yet. I'm afraid I will.

name: Santiago
text: [relieved] Thank you. You've stood beside me. I'll try to remember that when I start worrying again.

name: Santiago
text: [easier] I wrote to Mother. Told her about you. Left out the fighting, or she'd walk all the way here to fetch me.

name: Santiago
text: [fond] She has a bakery. I used to carry flour before dawn and complain about the weight. I'd give a good deal to be back there tomorrow morning.

name: Santiago
text: [warm] She's kept my stool by the oven. I used to sleep there between deliveries. Apparently my bedroom was too far away when she needed another sack.

name: Santiago
text: [shy] Yes. I'd like that. Could we take our time? There's still so much I don't know about you.

name: Santiago
text: [gentle] All right. I won't keep asking. Come and sit with me later, if you'd like.

name: Santiago
text: [nervous] I've been looking forward to our evenings together. Even when I'm too tired to say much.

name: Santiago
text: [earnest] Would you have supper with me when we get a night to ourselves? I'd like to take you somewhere decent.

name: Santiago
text: [pleased] Good. I know a place. And if I salute you at the table, please pretend you didn't see it.

name: Santiago
text: [bravely] All right. I'm glad you told me plainly. I won't bring it up again.

name: Santiago
text: [shouting] Dawning Flame, keep my hand steady!

name: Santiago
text: [earnest] Get behind my shield! Now!

name: Santiago
text: [strained] Caught the mail. I'm standing. Keep going!

name: Beau
text: [stammering, warm] You're — y-you're his. Tesfaye's. I'd know that coat anywhere; he w-wore it the day we met. Come in. Come in out of the road.

name: Beau
text: [quiet] Del. It's the ward. He sent the ward.

name: Beau
text: [low] Del. The p-paper the man on the steps had. Look at the seal. Iron hand, red wax.

name: Beau
text: [steadier] That's the mark on the ore wagons. The ones that come up from Dunmere and go north. I've seen it a hundred times at the ford.

name: Beau
text: [grim] Slaves. They're w-working slaves in there. I can hear the chains from here.

name: Beau
text: [steady] I'm going to the bottom for 'em, {target}. Whatever else we do today. Tell me you're with me.

name: Beau
text: [fierce] Good. G-good. The front's mine. Nothing gets past me today.

name: Beau
text: [quiet] There'll be time. I'll m-make time.

name: Beau
text: [urgent] The ch-chain-gang. Where do they keep them between shifts?

name: Beau
text: [shouting from below] Coming up! Nineteen of 'em and me! Hold the d-door — they're right behind us!

name: Beau
text: [exhausted] Nineteen. Every one. Not one left in the dark.

name: Beau
text: [quiet] Thank you for holding. I heard you say it. I won't forget it.

name: Beau
text: [steady] H-hold the line. Hold it. Nothing gets past.

name: Beau
text: [grunting] Shield's up. Hit 'em while they hit me.

name: Beau
text: [shouting] Del! Behind you!

name: Delphine
text: [warm, gentle] I'm Delphine, Beau's wife. Your late stepfather, Tesfaye, was an old friend of ours. Sit down, honey. Beau, get the good bread.

name: Delphine
text: [steady] He wrote to us from Lanternhold every year for twenty years. Said you and Hiwot were growing up in that keepers' library, getting into everything he tried to keep you out of. His last letter said if you came here without him, we were to keep you safe.

name: Delphine
text: [quiet, direct] So. How did he die? All of it. Don't you spare me.

name: Delphine
text: [very still] Black plate. Asked for you by name.

name: Delphine
text: [to Beau] Beau. The letter from the spring. He said if a big man in black iron ever came asking, we weren't to fight him, we were to run with the child and ask questions after. I thought he'd gone strange.

name: Delphine
text: [gently] That's a kindness, and a lie, and I'll take both. Thank you, sugar.

name: Delphine
text: [to Beau] Beau. Whoever did it knew where Tesfaye was, and Tesfaye chose that library because nobody knew. Somebody talked.

name: Delphine
text: [soft] Then don't. But you'll tell Beau when you can; he loved him too, and he's worse at waiting than I am.

name: Delphine
text: [looking] It is. The Iron Consortium's mark — the trading house out of the Gate that's been buying every bar on this coast since the ore went bad.

name: Delphine
text: [slowly] So the folks paying to kill Tesfaye's ward are the folks who own the iron. That ain't two stories, honey. That's one. Now you ask me whatever you need to, and then we decide what he'd have done.

name: Delphine
text: [matter-of-fact] Folks who keep the balance between the towns and the wild, and between the strong and the weak, when the law's too far off to do it. Tesfaye was one, before the library. So are we. It don't pay, and nobody thanks you, and you do it anyway. That's the whole of the oath.

name: Delphine
text: [carefully] I don't know, and I won't pretend I do. I know Tesfaye hid you like a man hides a lit candle in a wind, and never said from what. A trading house don't spend two hundred on spite. They think you're worth it, or they think you're dangerous, and I can't tell you which from here.

name: Delphine
text: [softening] He'd have followed the money. The iron's gone bad since spring — tools snapping, blades cracking, every smith from here to the Gate cussing — and the ore comes up out of Dunmere. The Consortium's mark is on the wagons and on your bounty. So we go to Dunmere and find out what's wrong with that ore, and I'd bet my house we find out who wants you dead the same day.

name: Delphine
text: [flat] You'll go with us or you'll go over my husband, and he's a big man. Tesfaye asked. I don't break a promise to a dead friend because a child is grieving and rude about it.

name: Delphine
text: [decisive] Beau, get the shields. We're going to Dunmere.

name: Delphine
text: [to you] I'll tell you what: you're Tesfaye's, and Tesfaye's is ours. That's all the reason we need, and it's all the reason you're getting tonight.

name: Delphine
text: [calm] Dunmere's two days south. Mining town, hard folk, honest as far as it goes. The mayor's a man called Gethin Pryce; he'll be sweating, and he'll pay.

name: Delphine
text: [dry] Stay off the river road after dark. Gnolls come down it. I know because I've buried the people who didn't listen.

name: Delphine
text: [casual, not casual] Hiwot. You grew up in that library with him. Did he keep letters? Anything from the Gate, anything with that iron seal on it?

name: Delphine
text: [nodding] Then it's still there. Remember that, both of you. If this road ever bends back toward Lanternhold, that drawer's the first door we open.

name: Delphine
text: [sharp] A year hunting one ogre alone, and the Wardens never heard of you. Why didn't you come to us?

name: Delphine
text: [a beat] ...It ain't. Damn it. It should be.

name: Delphine
text: [level] Gethin. Before the crews. Who's been buying your bad ore since spring, and who's been selling the smiths good iron since?

name: Delphine
text: [to Beau, quiet] Same hand. Beau, I told you. Buy the ore cheap because it's bad, sell the iron dear because it's the only good iron left. Somebody's making that ore bad on purpose.

name: Delphine
text: [calm] Mind the timbers; half of them are rotten. If the kobolds are as thick as the mayor says, we go slow and we keep the healer in the middle. That's me, honey. Don't argue.

name: Delphine
text: [calm] Water on the second level, and not from any spring. Somebody opened a channel and let the river in on purpose.

name: Delphine
text: [thoughtful] Kobolds don't plan. Kobolds dig where they're pointed. Whoever's pointing them is below us, and has been for weeks.

name: Delphine
text: [flat] Your orders. Sealed how? Iron hand, red wax, pressed hard.

name: Delphine
text: [to you, low] On a wagon, on a bounty, and now on an altar. That's three. — Go on, honey. He's yours to deal with.

name: Delphine
text: [reading] "To the priest, from Femi at the Thornbury inn. Keep the ore fouled until the spring shipment. Gorruk holds the north road; do not use it without his mark."

name: Delphine
text: [calm] A courier, and a bandit lord above him, and above them somebody who buys with a seal instead of a name. The mine was only the bottom of this.

name: Delphine
text: [after a moment] He was the best of us, sugar. And he quit. Those ain't two different stories either.

name: Delphine
text: [pleasant, deadly] Hollister says you've had that room since the spring, Femi. Now I'll tell you what puzzles me. What does a wine merchant sell for six months in a town with one inn, that already has a cellar?

name: Delphine
text: [to you] He's got papers, honey. I'd like to see them.

name: Delphine
text: [level] A name, Cal. Not a seal. Somebody at the Consortium signs for this. Who?

name: Delphine
text: [calm] The Mirkhollow. Old wood — older than the Wardens, older than the Gate. It's got its own druids, and they ain't friends of ours; we keep the balance by law and they keep it by blood.

name: Delphine
text: [quiet] Keep to the deer paths. Anything down here that looks like a road was made by something with a great many legs.

name: Delphine
text: [steady] None of us. The iron's what we took off the men who are poisoning your river. We're here to shut their mine.

name: Delphine
text: [calm] Iron livery on the guards. Consortium men. And the tall one — Kestrel. A sword for hire who'll guard anything for anybody. I've crossed him before.

name: Delphine
text: [flat] He won't talk. Don't waste your breath on it.

name: Delphine
text: [quiet] Sit a minute. The forest's loud tonight and I want to say a thing before I lose the nerve.

name: Delphine
text: [soft] Tesfaye wrote to us every year about you. Twenty letters. I feel like I've known you since you could walk, and I met you a month ago. It's a strange thing. It ain't an unwelcome one.

name: Delphine
text: [fond] The first year, that you'd learned to walk and walked straight into the library. The seventh, that you'd stolen honey from the brothers and let a cat take the blame. The last — that you were ready, and that he wasn't.

name: Delphine
text: [a soft laugh] Enough. Yeah. That's a very Tesfaye amount.

name: Delphine
text: [warm] Goodnight, {target}. Wake me if the trees start walking.

name: Delphine
text: [quiet] All right. Get some rest. We can talk another time.

name: Delphine
text: [calm] Goodnight.

name: Delphine
text: [fond] He is. He also snores like a bear in a barrel, so the fortune runs both ways.

name: Delphine
text: [warm] Goodnight, {target}. Don't you tell him I said that.

name: Delphine
text: [tight] Beau's still down there. {target}. Beau is still down there.

name: Delphine
text: [screaming] NO —

name: Delphine
text: [broken] He was coming up. He was coming up. You heard the chains. You heard him.

name: Delphine
text: [hollow] Olamide's papers. Names in the city. Take them. I don't care.

name: Delphine
text: [cold] I'll finish this road because Tesfaye asked it of me. Don't you speak to me until it's done.

name: Delphine
text: [reading] Olamide wrote to three men at the Consortium's tower in Varenholm's Gate. Adigun Adeyinka. Bankole. Rotimi.

name: Delphine
text: [calm] Adeyinka. Cal heard right. The bandits are broke and the mine's drowned, and the road north is open, and so, at last, are the names.

name: Delphine
text: [disturbed] That's the merchant's face and it ain't the merchant. Look at the eyes, honey. Nothing lives behind 'em.

name: Delphine
text: [hard] Shape-thieves. They wear you after they kill you. Don't let one get behind you.

name: Delphine
text: [murmuring] A clerk with a list and two guards who are paid to believe him.

name: Delphine
text: [quiet] He believed it. Third floor. Don't touch anything.

name: Delphine
text: [flat] Stairs, then.

name: Delphine
text: [reading] Adigun Adeyinka, Bankole, Rotimi. Gone to Lanternhold — to LANTERNHOLD — for a summit with the keepers.

name: Delphine
text: [cold] The three men behind all of this are sitting in the library you grew up in.

name: Delphine
text: [warm] You're family, honey. You don't have to face this alone. Get some rest. We leave for Lanternhold in the morning.

name: Delphine
text: [flat] Then answer me this, Adeyinka, before anybody decides anything. The iron hand in red wax on the ore wagons. Whose seal is that?

name: Delphine
text: [to you, quiet] Your seal on the wagons and his on the bounty. Same wax. I've been right since the inn, honey, and I ain't glad of it.

name: Delphine
text: [sharp] Two of 'em — and the real Hiwot was BEHIND it, {target}, you cut her — she's breathing. She's breathing. She ain't walking out of here on her own.

name: Delphine
text: [grim] I'll get her to the surface. Go on without us.

name: Delphine
text: [urgent] That ain't who it looks like. {target}. That is NOT them. It's already reaching for your throat — move!

name: Delphine
text: [grim] That wasn't him, and you knew it before I did. It's dead. There's two more behind it wearing faces I don't know — keep moving.

name: Delphine
text: [weary] The shore. Air. We're out.

name: Delphine
text: [hard] Sanni sent us after his father. Then he called the guards on us. With Adigun dead and us wanted for murder, who is left to stop him?

name: Delphine
text: [cold] Grand Duke Ayodele was murdered last night and they've put your name on it. Obi's dead too. A man called Segun Marr runs the Gauntlet now.

name: Delphine
text: [calm] Kolade will be sworn in as the new Duke within days. He's moved everything into place while we were underground.

name: Delphine
text: [calm] Three ways into that palace, and we won't get a second try.

name: Delphine
text: [measured] Adebayo's dying; cure him and the Gauntlet is ours. Folake offered a way in, for a price. And the thieves under the Undervault will sell us a door if we owe 'em after.

name: Delphine
text: [approving] Lawfully. Tesfaye would've said the same, and then he'd have cheated a little. Let's go find the Duke.

name: Delphine
text: [flat] Her. Fine. I'll hold my nose. Don't you let her hold anything of yours.

name: Delphine
text: [dry] Tunde Softfoot never forgets a debt. Neither will you. All right — the Undervault.

name: Delphine
text: [low] Borrowed silks, real steel, two invitations. Everybody in that hall is either a guest or a shape-thief, and there's no way to tell which till the knives come out.

name: Delphine
text: [calm] Stay near the dukes. He needs them dead more than he needs you.

name: Delphine
text: [shouting] The dukes are DYING, {target} — we can't hold both if you run at him —

name: Delphine
text: [flat] Where's Emeka Obi, Marr? He had a wife on Tanner Street. She'd like to know where to put the flowers.

name: Delphine
text: [low] A temple to a dead god, still swept, still lit. Somebody's been praying here for twenty years.

name: Delphine
text: [steady] Whatever he says at that altar, {target}, you remember who raised you. Then you do what you have to.

name: Delphine
text: [cold] Our faces. Every one. Kill 'em quick; don't look at the eyes.

name: Delphine
text: [calm] Breathe, honey. The one in front's slower than he looks.

name: Delphine
text: [sharp] Mind the mage. I'll mind the rest.

name: Delphine
text: [dry] If you die, I will be very put out. Don't.

name: Itsuki
text: [quiet, from the treeline] Forgive me. I do not mean to alarm you. I have walked beside your road for an hour, deciding whether to speak.

name: Itsuki
text: [level] You are going north to the Gate, by the river road? — Then I will be plain. I am Itsuki. A year ago an ogre called Gorruk, who leads the bandit companies in the north, burned a wagon on this road. My wife was in it. I have hunted him since, alone, and alone I cannot reach him.

name: Itsuki
text: [calm] I did. A man at a Warden house on the coast told me the north road is not the Wardens' road. He was polite about it.

name: Itsuki
text: [level] You are going towards him. I would go with you. I ask nothing else.

name: Itsuki
text: [thinking] I have seen letters carried to his camp. Sealed. I did not read them; I was too far, and I am no thief. The seal was red, and pressed hard. That is all I can say honestly.

name: Itsuki
text: [a long pause] Hana. Thank you for asking. No one asks. They ask about him.

name: Itsuki
text: [a small bow] Then I am in your debt before I have earned my place. I will keep the rear. You will not hear me unless you need to.

name: Itsuki
text: [calm] I understand. I will walk on ahead of you, then. If our roads cross again, I will not ask twice.

name: Itsuki
text: [very quiet] Gorruk. Where does he sleep?

name: Itsuki
text: [very quietly] {target}. I have him. A clean line, no cover. Say yes.

name: Itsuki
text: [exhaling] Thank you. Whatever comes after this — thank you.

name: Itsuki
text: [tight] Alive. I have waited a year. I can wait until the end of a fight.

name: Itsuki
text: [cold] He walked out of that tent because you wished it. I will find him myself.

name: Itsuki
text: [flat] Do not follow me.

name: Itsuki
text: [quietly] It is done. I thought I would feel taller. I feel as though I could sleep for a year.

name: Itsuki
text: [soft] I will stay, if you will have me. There is nothing else I was for.

name: Itsuki
text: [low] I have spent so long following tracks that I have given little thought to what comes after.

name: Itsuki
text: [tired] I cannot go back to the life I had with my wife. I do not yet know what else I want.

name: Itsuki
text: [quiet] I would like to stay. It helps to have people expecting me back.

name: Itsuki
text: [thoughtful] I used to guide travellers through the woods. Some had never slept outside. They would wake me over every rustle.

name: Itsuki
text: [faintly amused] One paid me extra to keep the owls away. I gave him something to plug his ears.

name: Itsuki
text: [warm] I would enjoy that. There are places worth visiting without a bounty to collect.

name: Itsuki
text: [careful] I care for you. I need time before I can promise more. If you are willing to wait, I would like to try.

name: Itsuki
text: [calm] Take the time you need. You know where to find me.

name: Itsuki
text: [low] I still miss my wife. I always will.

name: Itsuki
text: [quiet] But I have come to care for you too. If you feel the same, I would like us to be together.

name: Itsuki
text: [quiet] Then we will take our time. I am glad you told me.

name: Itsuki
text: [calm] I understand. It was enough to say it. Sleep.

name: Itsuki
text: [very quiet] The north road. A year ago. Were you there when the wagons burned?

name: Itsuki
text: [very quietly] Mine. You said. Say it again.

name: Itsuki
text: [quiet] Loosing.

name: Itsuki
text: [flat] The archer is mine. Leave him.

name: Itsuki
text: [cold] Again.

name: Bahadır
text: [booming] — and I say AGAIN, red man, you touch that cage and I will fold you into it!

name: Bahadır
text: [turning] VALLAHI. Strangers. Good. Strangers, listen: Bahadır, ranger of Kalden, and this is Fındık, who is small but very brave. There is a woman in that fortress, in a cage. Yasemin. A witch of my country, and a good one.

name: Bahadır
text: [hot] Tell them why Vashk burns women, wizard! Tell them what your Crimson masters do with a witch's bones!

name: Bahadır
text: [overjoyed] With you! Yes! Fındık, did you hear? We have friends, and they are good ones. Come — the gate is that way, and I am going through it.

name: Bahadır
text: [wounded, roaring] You TOOK his coin. You looked at me and you took his coin! Then you go through me, and Fındık, and every tree in this valley — come on! COME ON!

name: Bahadır
text: [emphatic] We are yours, {target}. Vallahi. Where you go, we go, and anyone who says otherwise answers to Fındık.

name: Bahadır
text: [roaring] FINDIK SAYS GO FOR THE EYES!

name: Bahadır
text: [booming] Nobody touches the witch! NOBODY! Vallahi!

name: Bahadır
text: [gleeful] Ha HA! Did you SEE that, canım?

name: Yasemin
text: [cold, from the cage] Thank you. I would kneel, but the bars have made it difficult.

name: Yasemin
text: [looking at you] You. Come closer. Something in your blood woke when you came through the fortress gate; I felt it through the bars like heat from a stove in the next room. I have read auras all my life and I have never felt one like it.

name: Yasemin
text: [direct] So tell me, before I decide what to do about it. When it woke — what did it want?

name: Yasemin
text: [a slow nod] Honest. Good. Then I know what kind of thing it is, if not its name: something that was worshipped once, and fed. I would sooner walk beside it than behind it. Bahadır goes where I go, and Fındık goes where Bahadır goes, and so you have three. Two and a half.

name: Yasemin
text: [dry] You felt nothing. Canım, I watched your hand. — Very well; you are not ready to say it, and that is your right. I will walk beside you anyway, and I will keep watching the hand. Bahadır goes where I go.

name: Yasemin
text: [precise] Something that was worshipped once, and should not have been. That is as plain as I can be without lying to you. I read auras, not histories. Now answer mine.

name: Yasemin
text: [dry] As you like. I am a witch. Keeping things to myself is most of the work. I will walk beside you, and I will not say it again in front of the others. Bahadır goes where I go.

name: Yasemin
text: [calm] Frost. Hold him still.

name: Yasemin
text: [formal] Your aura flares when you fight. Interesting.

name: Yasemin
text: [cool] Keep them in front of us.

name: Devendra
text: [disdainful] Kindly disregard the large gentleman; his enthusiasms are exhausting. Devendra, Crimson Wizard of Vashk. The woman in the cage is a Kalden witch, and it is quite evident that a Kalden witch loose in these hills is a calamity waiting for a date.

name: Devendra
text: [coolly] Vashk and Kalden have been at war, in one form or another, since before these strangers' grandparents were born. I do not expect the large gentleman to understand policy. I expect him to understand a hundred in gold — which I am offering to you, not to him. A hundred to see her burned, and my considerable talents beside you until the Gate.

name: Devendra
text: [coolly] Because one witch becomes a coven, and a coven becomes a border dispute, and a border dispute becomes my problem. That I am polite about it is a courtesy, not a change of policy.

name: Devendra
text: [satisfied] A sensible arrangement. The large gentleman will object; I recommend we not be near him when he does.

name: Devendra
text: [thin] Hold my tongue. Very well. I shall hold it most eloquently. Do not expect me to be happy about it.

name: Devendra
text: [bored] Do kindly keep them off me; I am the expensive one.

name: Devendra
text: [smug] Burning. Obviously.

name: Devendra
text: [sneering] Barely worth the spell.

name: Layla
text: [cold] Yes. Stare. A dark elf, above ground, in daylight. You will not see another.

name: Layla
text: [contemptuous] I am a priestess, and a fugitive, and there is a bounty on me that these three would like to collect. I cured a village of the coughing sickness on my way here. They are arresting me for having the wrong face. Decide what that makes you.

name: Layla
text: [level] Of a goddess your Order has no name for, boy, and would not like if it did. Does it change your sword arm?

name: Layla
text: [flat] My own people. I refused a thing that was asked of me, and among my kind refusal is answered with a knife. I came up into the light because there was nowhere left to go down. I have not found the light kinder, ya stranger. Only brighter.

name: Layla
text: [surprised] Protection. From you. How strange, and how useful.

name: Layla
text: [dry] Very well. By the deep, I go where you go, until I decide otherwise. Try to be interesting.

name: Layla
text: [flat] Of course. Walk on. Everyone does.

name: Layla
text: [venomous] You will remember this. I will see that you do, from wherever they put me.

name: Layla
text: [cold] Well? You have looked long enough to decide.

name: Layla
text: [low, amused] Answer her. She is the only person in this tower telling the truth, and she is doing it for money. I respect that.

name: Layla
text: [direct] I appreciate what you did for me. Understand something, though. You did not buy my loyalty by keeping me alive.

name: Layla
text: [firm] I choose where I go and whom I serve.

name: Layla
text: [approving] Good. I prefer travelling with someone who understands that.

name: Layla
text: [unguarded] I miss the quiet of the shrine. Before the petitions began, I had an hour to myself.

name: Layla
text: [dry] Up here, someone is always shouting, selling something, or telling me what a lovely morning it is. Usually in the rain.

name: Layla
text: [measured] The work was demanding. I liked that. I knew what was expected of me, and I was good at it. I miss having a place of my own.

name: Layla
text: [interested] You have my attention. Let us spend more time together before deciding anything.

name: Layla
text: [level] Then leave it for now. You can bring it up when you know what you want.

name: Layla
text: [dry] I enjoy your company when you stop trying to give me orders.

name: Layla
text: [direct] I would like some time alone with you. Interested?

name: Layla
text: [pleased] Good. Come and sit with me. Your duties can wait for an evening.

name: Layla
text: [cool] Very well. I will not ask again.

name: Layla
text: [amused] Guess.

name: Layla
text: [approving] Ruthless. Correct. The real one is breathing behind it; someone drag her out.

name: Layla
text: [sharp] That is not your kin. Kill it before it kisses you.

name: Layla
text: [approving] Good. You did not even let it finish. There are more behind it; kill them the same way.

name: Layla
text: [reverent] Do you feel it? The stone remembers him. Morrak. By the deep — it would remember you too, if you let it.

name: Layla
text: [contemptuous] Bleed, then, if you must.

name: Layla
text: [cool] Wound them. I will decide who heals.

name: Layla
text: [dry] Surface-dwellers. Always the front lane.

name: Kaito
text: [cheerful, from above] Ah — hello. Yes. Up here. In the web. It is exactly as embarrassing as it looks, and I apologise for it.

name: Kaito
text: [appraising] Not bounty hunters; you walk too close together. A green sash — Wardens, then, or with Wardens. Good. Wardens cut people down for nothing. Kaito. I hunt bounties, mostly, and I was hunting a wyvern's head when the spiders took offence.

name: Kaito
text: [bright] The magistrate of Thornbury, whose sheep keep disappearing. Three hundred in gold, and — I am told — the gratitude of a woman with a very fine face. I am still negotiating the second part.

name: Kaito
text: [delighted] Ah. Now we are talking properly. My bow, until your road ends. And a thing I saw, which I think you will want: east of here, past the wyvern cliffs, there is a mine under the hill. Men in iron livery go in at dawn and men in chains come out at dusk. I did not go closer. I hunt beasts. That did not look like a beast.

name: Kaito
text: [relieved] You are my favourite person. I say that to everyone. This once, forgive me, I mean it.

name: Kaito
text: [smiling] I will come along, if you will have me. The wyverns are that way, and so, I suspect, is whatever you came into these woods to find.

name: Kaito
text: [calling after you] Fair enough! If you change your mind, I will be — well. Here.

name: Kaito
text: [bright] There she is. The matriarch. That head is worth three hundred in gold and a magistrate's gratitude, and I intend, respectfully, to collect both.

name: Kaito
text: [murmuring] Doorman. Big. Bored. I can talk us past him; bored men love a story, and I have several.

name: Kaito
text: [pleased] — and that is how I lost the boot. He is still laughing. In, in, before he thinks about it.

name: Kaito
text: [resigned] Through him. Very well. I will apologise to him afterwards; it seems only polite.

name: Kaito
text: [murmuring] A clerk. A list. Two guards. Forgive me — I love a lobby.

name: Kaito
text: [smiling] He believed it. Third floor. Touch nothing, he says — as if.

name: Kaito
text: [cheerful] Stairs it is.

name: Kaito
text: [quieter] I know I make a performance of everything. It is easier than admitting I was scared.

name: Kaito
text: [honest] When you found me, I thought I was going to die there. I have been sleeping badly since.

name: Kaito
text: [soft] Thank you. I might be rather poor company tonight, but I would like you to stay.

name: Kaito
text: [cheerful] I used to play for supper at roadside inns. I know six songs well and about forty badly.

name: Kaito
text: [smiling] I still have the lute. I sold the feathered hat. A man has to improve himself somehow.

name: Kaito
text: [amused] Cruel, but fair. I will play you the good six. You can request the others after enough wine.

name: Kaito
text: [pleased] I was hoping you might say that. Let us have a little time together and see how we get on.

name: Kaito
text: [easy] All right. Let me know if you want to try again. No awkwardness between us.

name: Kaito
text: [smiling] I like you. I'd like to spend an evening with you, without the rest of this lot.

name: Kaito
text: [delighted] Excellent. A decent meal, some wine, and no work.

name: Kaito
text: [warm] I have been looking forward to this.

name: Kaito
text: [light] Stop it is. Friends, then, and I am very good at that as well.

name: Kaito
text: [wincing] Right call, wrong result — the real Hiwot was behind it. She is breathing. I will carry her out; go.

name: Kaito
text: [breathless] Not him — and you knew. It is down. Two more behind it, and I do not like their faces either.

name: Kaito
text: [shouting] Not them! NOT them! It has teeth, {target}!

name: Kaito
text: [hushed] The thieves' maze. Every third flagstone is a trap and every fourth is a thief. I know the path; follow my feet exactly, please.

name: Kaito
text: [murmuring] Left. Left. Do not step there. — And we are through, and nobody even bled. I love being right.

name: Kaito
text: [sighing] Straight through. Watch the flagstones, then, and try to bleed on the thieves and not on me.

name: Kaito
text: [smiling] Loosing, loosing — got him, and he was handsome, too. A pity.

name: Kaito
text: [cheerful] Behind them! I am behind them!

name: Kaito
text: [light] If I die, tell the magistrate I was thinking of her.

name: Wanjiru
text: [fierce] Far enough. This wood is not a road, and you are not welcome on it. The Umbra hold this grove, and the Umbra say turn around. Eh?

name: Wanjiru
text: [sniffing] You carry iron from the Gate. The wood smells it on you. Which of you is theirs?

name: Wanjiru
text: [narrowing] A Warden says so. Wardens said so about the last mine, and the last mine is still there.

name: Wanjiru
text: [low] Mzee Kamau would sooner have you bleed than speak. I would sooner hear you first. So. Speak.

name: Wanjiru
text: [low] No answer. Then hear this: the Mzee would sooner have you bleed than speak. I would sooner hear you first. Speak, or turn around.

name: Wanjiru
text: [bitter] Dead fish for a mile downstream. Stags with sores on their flanks. And men — men in chains, walking into a hole in the hill every dawn, and fewer walking out. The wood knows what is being done to it. It does not know how to stop it. I do.

name: Wanjiru
text: [grudging] Then we want the same thing, and I would rather kill them beside you than argue with the Mzee about killing you.

name: Wanjiru
text: [decisive] Sawa. I am coming. He can take it up with the trees.

name: Wanjiru
text: [snarling] Then the roots will have you. MZEE! Kamau! They have chosen!

name: Wanjiru
text: [quiet] So this is the mine.

name: Wanjiru
text: [hard] For two years, I have watched the river get worse. Dead fish, sick animals. All because of this place.

name: Wanjiru
text: [firm] I want this mine shut before we leave.

name: Wanjiru
text: [snarling] The roots have him.

name: Wanjiru
text: [fierce] Trees do not forgive. Neither do I.

name: Wanjiru
text: [low] Bleed into the soil. Good. Sawa.

name: Dai Morgan
text: [gravelly, Welsh] Well now. Either you're the new drivers or the old ones are dead. Which is it, then? — No, don't tell me; you're too muddy for drivers, and they'd have shot me by now.

name: Dai Morgan
text: [hopeful] Dai Morgan. Priest of the deep places, and the last of the clan that cut this mine before the Consortium took it with paper and knives. I know every valve in it — including the one at the bottom that lets the river in.

name: Dai Morgan
text: [grim] Bottom level, by the valve room, so the drivers can drown them if the mine's ever taken. Mind that, shield-man. Whoever turns that wheel turns it on them.

name: Dai Morgan
text: [grim] A debt we didn't owe, bought off a man who didn't own it, and enforced by men with swords while the magistrate looked at the ceiling. My cousins argued. My cousins are on the lowest level now, and they don't argue anymore.

name: Dai Morgan
text: [grunting to his feet] With you. Aye. There's lovely. Mind the third level; the mage keeps his study there, and he doesn't care for knocking.

name: Dai Morgan
text: [flat] Come back for me. Aye. Everybody says that, bach.

name: Dai Morgan
text: [very level] Morgan. Bryn and Gareth Morgan. My cousins. Which ledger are they in, mage?

name: Dai Morgan
text: [quiet] ...Then I'll be having ledger four. Go on, {target}.

name: Dai Morgan
text: [urgent] The valve room. Turn the great wheel and the river takes the bottom two levels in the time it takes to say a prayer.

name: Dai Morgan
text: [hard] Your shield-man went below for the chain-gang. He isn't up yet.

name: Dai Morgan
text: [hopeful] So. Are you letting me out, or are you the polite sort of drivers?

name: Dai Morgan
text: [approving] Good stonework, mind. Dwarven, some of it, and old. Shame about the smell.

name: Dai Morgan
text: [gravelly] Clerk with a list. Two guards. Good stone, again. Shame.

name: Dai Morgan
text: [grunting] Third floor. Don't touch anything. Good advice for a tower, that.

name: Dai Morgan
text: [grim] Stairs.

name: Dai Morgan
text: [gravelly] Wall. I'm the wall, I am.

name: Dai Morgan
text: [grunting] Hit 'em. I've got 'em.

name: Dai Morgan
text: [calm] The deep places keep me. Keep going, bach.

name: Amara
text: [quiet] You kept your word. Thank you for letting me help.

name: Amara
text: [steady] Put the swords away. If I wanted you dead I would have done it from the rooftop.

name: Amara
text: [grave] I am Amara. I love Kolade Adeyinka. I also helped him kill the man who raised you. I know what that makes me to you. But I need you to hear me. Have you ever loved someone even after you knew what they'd done?

name: Amara
text: [a slow nod] Then you know the shape of it. Good. I will not have to explain the rest, only ask it.

name: Amara
text: [quiet] Yes. Kolade has lied to me too. I know he has hurt people. I still care for him, but I cannot let him go on killing.

name: Amara
text: [level] Then you will think what I ask is weakness. Hear it anyway; you may need it later, when you are older and less certain.

name: Amara
text: [without flinching] No. I was not. But I did not stop him sending Gorruk north, and I could have. Put that on my account with the rest, ranger. I will not argue the sum.

name: Amara
text: [grave] Here is what I ask. Stop him. Not kill him. Stop him. There is a difference, and it matters to me more than my own life.

name: Amara
text: [exact] Chains, and a cell, and the Council's law. He is not a god yet. He bleeds, he tires, he can be beaten to his knees; I have seen it done, once, in the fire temple where we met. On his knees he can be bound. It is not a small thing I ask. I know that.

name: Amara
text: [exhaling] Thank you. I did not expect that.

name: Amara
text: [quiet] The coronation is in three nights. Two people called Rasheed and Kemi hold the invitations in the Undervault. Take them from them; they will not give them up.

name: Amara
text: [cold] Then we will meet at the gate of the Undercity, and one of us will not walk past the other.

name: Amara
text: [flat] Rasheed and Kemi hold the invitations. Undervault. Take them; it does not change what I said.

name: Amara
text: [searching] ...Your word. Yes. — Rasheed and Kemi, the Undervault. The invitations. Go.

name: Amara
text: [quiet] I said one of us would not walk past the other.

name: Amara
text: [steady] I am still asking. Stop him. Do not kill him. And if you cannot promise me that, then draw, because I will not let you reach him without it.

name: Amara
text: [sad] Then draw.

name: Amara
text: [stepping aside] Go. I will be at the altar before you, on my knees, asking him the same thing. He will not listen to me. He might listen to you.

name: Amara
text: [startled] With — yes. Yes. I know the way; I have walked it a hundred times. Stay behind me at the stairs.

name: Amara
text: [searching your face] ...Go, then. If you are lying, I will know it at the altar.

name: Amara
text: [kneeling] Kolade. Please. Look at me. It does not have to be the altar. It can be a cell and a window and me visiting every week for the rest of your life.

name: Amara
text: [exact] Two blades. Two throats. Next.

name: Amara
text: [steady] Watch the flank. I have the front.

name: Amara
text: [quiet] Not like this. Quickly. Clean.
